item.title: How an ancient resin traded for centuries got snarled up by the Iran war
item.summary: It's not just energy supplies that have been disrupted by the Iran war. It's also hitting frankincense, a commodity that's been defining trade routes in the Middle East for thousands of years.

item.title: What draws people into cults? A new book tracks the journeys of two followers
item.summary: Harrison Hill's book The Oracle's Daughter is a story about the terror of losing the self — but it's also, gratifyingly, a story about finding the way back to it.

item.title: Melania Trump denies close ties to Jeffrey Epstein in rare public statement
item.summary: The first lady made a rare public statement on Thursday saying she was not friends with the late sex offender. She also said Epstein did not introduce her to President Donald Trump.

item.title: 710,000 fewer babies were born last year in U.S. compared with two decades ago
item.summary: The U.S. fertility rate continued its slide to historic levels, due to plunging teen pregnancies and far more women delaying motherhood into their 30s and 40s.

item.title: The most memorable moon movies aren't even about space
item.summary: While marveling at Artemis II's mission, NPR's film critic went down a rabbit hole about moon-themed movies. Most have nothing to do with space.

item.title: How a cheese sandwich at the Masters is still $1.50 in an era of price hikes
item.summary: The priciest concessions at the Masters, beer and wine, cost just $6 each. The Georgia golf tournament prides itself on a simple and affordable menu, even as ticket prices continue to climb.

item.title: How bad for humans is wildlife trade? A new study has answers
item.summary: People sell wild animals for food and for traditional medicine — legally and illegally. A study looks at the risks of spillover diseases from those pangolins, giant rats and other exotic critters.

item.title: We can't all be astronauts, but the Artemis II crew has fitness lessons for everyone
item.summary: The Artemis II astronauts don't have a lot of space to exercise. That's why they've got the flywheel — a small device that can be used for strength and cardio workouts.

item.title: Earl Sweatshirt and MIKE put a ring on indie rap's favorite friendship
item.summary: A much-hyped double album finds the two reveling in a mutual influence that has bloomed for a decade, shaping a scene in the process.

item.title: 'After the Flood' argues Bob Dylan's late career is just as potent as his early years
item.summary: Much of our image of Dylan derives from his early protest music, but Robert Polito's book makes the argument that the most recent 30 years of Dylan's career have been just as creative as the first 30.
